title: Coarsen predicate-lock promotion further: page 8->32, relation 4->16
configuration_cause: max_pred_locks_per_page=2 and max_pred_locks_per_relation=-2 (default) force early SIRead promotion to coarser granularity; the r005 test raised them to 8/4 and cut locks_total.p95 by ~80% and GetUserTweets.p99 by ~47-72%, but the TPS prediction was refuted because the amplitude was too small to move the terminal-bound GetUserTweets path.
mechanism: SERIALIZABLE SIRead locks are promoted to coarser granularity when per-page/per-relation caps are exceeded. r005 showed the promotion path is real: locks_total.p95 fell ~80% and GetUserTweets.p99 fell 47-72% with page=8/relation=4, yet TPS was inconclusive because the effect was within run-to-run noise. Raising the caps further (page 32, relation 16) keeps the same mechanism but with a larger amplitude, so the lock-bookkeeping reduction should be measurable in locks_total.p95 and GetUserTweets.p99 while lock_waiting_backends stays at 0 (no true lock contention, only bookkeeping).
query_effect: GetUserTweets is the terminal-dominant transaction (terminal_capacity_fraction 0.88). Coarser SIRead locking reduces per-call lock bookkeeping on its read path, lowering its p99 and freeing terminal capacity.
expected_tps_effect: Small positive: successful_transaction_tps should rise modestly as GetUserTweets terminal occupancy drops; magnitude bounded by the 0.88 terminal fraction and the fact that lock bookkeeping is a secondary cost.
expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p99 should decrease; p50 roughly unchanged since promotion affects tail bookkeeping more than the median path.

predictions.rationale: Larger caps delay promotion, further reducing total SIRead lock count versus the r005 8/4 setting.
r005 already showed 47-72% p99 reduction at 8/4; larger amplitude should preserve or extend that direction.
Freed terminal capacity from lower GetUserTweets tail should translate to a small TPS gain; r005 was inconclusive at 8/4, so larger amplitude is the test.

alternatives.statement: If locks_total.p95 falls but GetUserTweets.p99 and TPS are unchanged, SIRead bookkeeping is not on the critical path and the terminal bottleneck is elsewhere (e.g. index scan cost).
If lock_waiting_backends.max rises above 0, coarser promotion is creating real serialization conflicts rather than reducing bookkeeping.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent sits at page=2/relation=-2 (defaults). r005 proved the promotion mechanism is real (locks_total.p95 -80%, GetUserTweets.p99 -47-72%) but was inconclusive on TPS due to small amplitude. This proposal keeps the same mechanism with a larger safe amplitude (page 32, relation 16) to make the TPS effect measurable.

nodes.label: Delayed SIRead promotion reduces per-txn predicate-lock bookkeeping

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 4x the r005 tested value of 8, within safe [0,256]; r005 showed -80% locks_total.p95 at 8, so 32 tests a larger amplitude of the same supported mechanism.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: page-level predicate-lock granularity cap; higher value delays promotion to coarser granularity

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 4x the r005 tested value of 4, within safe [-2,4096]; positive cap of 16 relation-level locks coarsens promotion further than r005's 4.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: relation-level predicate-lock granularity cap; higher positive value delays relation-level promotion
